newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: CRICKET-SOUTH AFRICA SET TO RECALL ADAMS.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-SOUTH AFRICA SET TO RECALL ADAMS.

text.p: Having pummelled India with pace in the first test in Durban South Africa are likely to add the guile of wrist spinner Paul Adams to their side for the second test which begins in Cape Town on Thursday.

India lost the opening match in the three-test series by 328 runs as they were skittled out by South Africa's four-pronged pace attack for 100 and 66 -- the latter the lowest total recorded against South Africa.
With the Newlands wicket expected to offer more turn, however, South Africa are prepared to change a winning team and recall Adams on his home ground.
The unorthodox spinner was South Africa's leading wicket taker on their recent Indian tour with 14 wickets in the three tests.
The team will be chosen from a squad of 13 on the morning of the match.
"We will have a look at the wicket before making our choice but Paul Adams is a strike bowler and he is central to our thinking," South African coach Bob Woolmer told Reuters.
"It will be a question of whether we play five bowlers or six batters and who we might leave out to allow Paul to play."

Pace bowler Lance Klusener is expected to make way for Adams, while Herschelle Gibbs is likely to give way after three inconclusive tests and allow his Western Province team mate Jacques Kallis to make his debut in the batting line-up.
India are expected to make only one change from the side humbled at Kingsmead.
Bowler Doda Ganesh is tipped to replace David Johnson as the third seam bowler while opener Vikram Rathore is to be given another chance to prove himself.
Rathore made only seven and two in the first test and failed again with nine in India's one-day defeat in a hastily arranged practice match against Natal on Monday.

He was expected to be replaced as opener by wicket-keeper Nayan Mongia, with V.V.S. Laxman the new man in the middle order. However, the Indian management are understood to prefer sparing Mongia the dual responsibilities.
Skipper Sachin Tendulkar told reporters: "We definitely need to resolve the issue about the openers but there comes a time when you have to stick with a combination."
India are likely to promote the composed Rahul Dravid to the problematical number three position, with Saurav Ganguly moving down to number six.
A pitch likely to offer turn will suit the leg spin of Indian vice-captain Anil Kumble.
"We expect them to bounce back and I am sure they will bat a lot more resolutely than they did in the first game," Woolmer said.
South Africa: Gary Kirsten, Andrew Hudson, Adam Bacher, Daryll Cullinan, Hansie Cronje (captain), Jacques Kallis, Brian McMillan, Shaun Pollock, Dave Richardson, Allan Donald, Paul Adams.
India: Vikram Rathore, Woorkeri Raman, Rahul Dravid, Sachin Tendulkar (captain), Mohammed Azharuddin, Saurav Ganguly, Nayan Mongia, Anil Kumble, Javagal Srinath, Venkatesh Prasad, Doda Ganesh.
